The app lists and releases are fetched again, a flake\'s inputs go to their newest (its flake.lock is updated), and a configuration.nix alone gets the newest nixpkgs; then the config is built, as Build does.
Open Nixup in the main user

This copy of Nixup runs in an app clone, work profile or another user. Magisk gives root only to the phone owner\'s apps, so here it is refused without asking. Open Nixup from the main user\'s home screen (not the clone\'s icon). Reinstalling the module removes this copy.

resources.string: the phone, picking up what a restart broke off
Clone its submodules too (private ones use the same token)

The repository: https://github.com/you/phone, github:you/phone or you/phone (GitHub), or any git address. It is cloned into Nixup\'s own folder (/data/adb/nixup/git); the terminal can change files there. A token is kept where only root reads it, as Nix\'s for the same site.
Not a repository address: like https://github.com/you/phone or you/phone, with no spaces or quotes; the other fields take letters, digits and . _ / -.
The clone of %1$s goes, with anything changed in it on this phone.
The clone is made again from %1$s, as the repository has it: what was changed in it on this phone goes.
The token could not be kept.
Removes the Nix packages Nixup keeps that the last build does not use (older generations\' ones, a service turned off). Going back to an older generation fetches its packages again.
It is downloaded from Nixup\'s releases and checked first: Nixup\'s module, newer, with its app signed by the same key as the app on this phone. The phone uses it from its next restart.

Google\'s sign-in page cannot load: this app has no internet. Either the phone is offline, or Network access is off for Nixup (App info, Mobile data and Wi-Fi, Network access). Turn it on, then come back here; once you are signed in it can go off again (the downloads do not need it).
Google\'s sign-in page did not load (%1$s). Is the phone online, and Network access on for Nixup (App info, Mobile data and Wi-Fi)?

No account is signed in. A build whose config lists apps from Google Play (android.packages.playstore) stops until one is.\n\nSign in here, on Google\'s own page, or give the config the account\'s token (android.playstore.tokenFile; nixup-play-login makes one on a PC). The phone keeps the token where root alone reads it. Better an account of its own for this: Google may block an account that downloads with an unofficial client.

Signed in as %1$s: the config\'s apps from Google Play (android.packages.playstore) are its downloads.\n\nShow token gives its token, for a config on a PC. Sign out takes it off the phone; Google\'s account page (Security, Your devices) can end its sign-in too.
The token of %1$s goes from the phone, and a build whose config lists apps from Google Play stops until an account signs in again.

Signed in as %1$s. This is the account\'s token: give it to a config on a PC (android.playstore.tokenFile), and each build puts it on the phone, which then needs no sign-in. Anyone who has it can use the account: keep it private, and delete a saved copy once it is in your config.
In the config, with the token in google-play.token next to it:
